### MAJOR SITE-21: The site's own scripts throw 1 error on 41 pages

**Why it matters:** An error nothing catches stops the script that threw it: whatever it was doing (a form's checks, a cart, tracking) is left undone. Visitors never report it; it is seen only in the browser's console.

**Likely fix:** Open the page with the browser's developer tools, read the console, and fix each error where its stack points.

### MINOR SITE-03: 4 of the site's own links redirect before they arrive

**Why it matters:** Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.

**Likely fix:** Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

- /dir: 301 to /dir/
- /verus-ai-new/: 301 to /verus-ai/
- /news-resources/leo-technologies-partners-with-deliverfund-to-fight-human-trafficking/: 301 to /leo-technologies-partners-with-deliverfund-to-fight-human-trafficking/
- /verus/: 301 to /verus-ai/

### MINOR SITE-24: 4 security headers no page sends

**Why it matters:** Each header closes off one way the site could be misused (a downgrade to http, a script slipped in, the site framed in another to trick a click). A missing one is a weaker defence, not a sign the site has been attacked; security reviews ask for them, and each costs a line of server configuration.

**Likely fix:** Add the missing headers in the web server or the CDN (one setting each), starting with Strict-Transport-Security.

- /: no page of the site sends Strict-Transport-Security (without it, browsers are not told to keep to https)
- /: no page of the site sends Content-Security-Policy (without it, nothing limits which scripts a page may run)
- /: no page of the site sends X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (without it, another site can frame the page to trick a click)
- /: no page of the site sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (without it, a browser may guess a file's type from its content)

### MINOR SITE-15: 3 pages have no main heading

**Why it matters:** Screen reader users jump to the h1 to learn what a page is, and search engines read it as the page's subject; none, or several competing, says neither.

**Likely fix:** Give each page one h1 naming what it shows; the site's name in the header is not it.

- /dir/: no h1 with words shown
- /dir-cpo-6149/: no h1 with words shown
- /partners/aws-partner/: no h1 with words shown

### MINOR SITE-03: 1 of the site's own links in a closed part of the page redirects before it arrives

**Why it matters:** Each is linked only from a part of the page that is closed when it loads (a menu, a tab, an answer that opens on a click, a link shown on hover): the crawler cannot tell whether a visitor opens it, so these are said apart, and as minor. Every click on one of these links costs an extra round trip before the page starts loading, and search engines see one page at two addresses.

**Likely fix:** Link to each page's final address (with or without its trailing slash, as the server serves it).

- /aws-partner: 301 to /partners/aws-partner/

### MINOR SITE-35: Requests to 1 host of other sites failed during the crawl, as seen from the crawler's machine and network

**Why it matters:** A script on the page asked another site's host for data (a third party's logging, analytics or a widget) and got an error or no answer. This was seen from the crawler's own machine and network only: an ad blocker, the region, DNS filtering or the crawler's own network can cause the same failure, and it may not fail for real visitors. The crawl cannot tell whether a page needs the answer. Where the crawl looked the name up from here, the line says so; "does not resolve" is stronger than "the request failed" (the host is probably gone), but it too is seen from here. It stops no build and no test.

**Likely fix:** If a name does not resolve, the host is probably gone: remove its snippet or tag from the site. Otherwise open the page from an ordinary browser and network; if the request works there, there is nothing to fix.

- /: `vimeo.com`: 4 pages asked it for data and the request failed (404); the name resolves from here, so the request failed for another reason

### MINOR SITE-29: The site publishes no security.txt, the file that tells security researchers whom to contact

**Why it matters:** Researchers who find a security problem look for /.well-known/security.txt to know whom to tell (RFC 9116); without it they may not report it, or report it publicly.

**Likely fix:** Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact line (an email address or a form) and an Expires line.

- /.well-known/security.txt: answered 404

### INFO SITE-40: 5 errors came from a source the crawl could not tell on 4 pages, as seen by an automated visitor: unconfirmed (no script was named as their source); check in a browser

**Why it matters:** An error whose stack names no script cannot be traced to the site or to another site: "A network error occurred." is the browser's own word for a request that failed, and the crawler blocks fonts, video and ad hosts, and meets bot challenges, that a person's browser does not, so it is not said as the site's.

**Likely fix:** Open the page in an ordinary browser with the developer tools' network tab and console. If the request fails there too, check the embed's address and the account with that service, or remove the embed. An error that shows in the console there too names its script there: fix it at that line.

- /: 2 errors of no known source: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 11 (line 1 column 12)
- /about/: 1 error of no known source: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 11 (line 1 column 12)
